Investors wipe $2.5T off Nasdaq as blue tsunami prompts AI fears reuters.com · 32 points · 9 comments · HN thread The article could not be read, so this summary is based on the title and the discussion. TL;DR A Reuters report says Nasdaq lost about $2.5 trillion in value after the 2026 midterm elections produced a Democratic sweep, with AI and data center stocks sliding on concerns about expansion plans. The article could not be read, so this summary rests on the headline, URL and comments. Headline says investors wiped $2.5 trillion off the Nasdaq after a 'blue tsunami' election result. Reported selloff is attributed to fears for AI and data center stocks and their expansion plans. The URL dates the story to November 5, 2026. Two related HN threads describe Nasdaq falling about 4% into correction territory. Discussion The thread is small and mostly argues about why data center and AI stocks might fall after a Democratic election sweep. One commenter says the drop is ordinary market dynamics with no conspiracy involved. Others treat the political angle as a shift in public sentiment against data centers, and a few mock the idea that Democrats are anti-tech. The mood is skeptical and somewhat combative, with more jabs than data. Market drop is normal rotation, not a political plot (some): One commenter argues that stocks often move inversely to good news and that a fall signals a change in market dynamics, not a conspiracy tied to who governs. Opposition is public sentiment against data centers (some): Commenters say voters across parties oppose local data centers over environmental and NIMBY concerns, so the Democratic label is incidental. Calling Democrats anti-tech is absurd (a few): Several replies mock the label with analogies, arguing that a stance on one issue does not make a party anti-tech or anti-life. Slowing AI through data center limits is short-sighted (a few): One commenter describes a Reddit thread where restricting data centers is framed as a way to slow AI, and argues research would not stop anyway. Sismo de magnitud 6.1 sacude Sinaloa; reportan epicentro cerca de Guasave Un sismo de magnitud 6.1 se registró al suroeste de Guasave, Sinaloa, con una profundidad de cinco kilómetros. El movimiento ocurrió el 30 de junio de 2026 y generó réplicas en la región. Por Gabriela Díaz | Reportera Un sismo de magnitud 6.1 se registró frente a las costas de Sinaloa, con epicentro localizado a 116 kilómetros al suroeste de Guasave, informó el Servicio Sismológico Nacional (SSN). El movimiento telúrico ocurrió el 30 de junio de 2026, a las 13:45:36 horas, tiempo del centro de México, con una profundidad de cinco kilómetros. El fenómeno fue reportado en una región del Golfo de California. Durante las horas posteriores se registraron movimientos adicionales, por lo que las autoridades mantuvieron el monitoreo de la actividad sísmica. SSN reporta réplicas después del sismo en Guasave El Servicio Sismológico Nacional informó que hasta las 15:00 horas del 30 de junio se habían registrado 10 réplicas del movimiento principal, cuya magnitud fue de 6.1. La réplica de mayor intensidad alcanzó una magnitud de 4.9, de acuerdo con los reportes difundidos por el organismo. Las réplicas son movimientos sísmicos que ocurren después de un temblor principal, debido al reajuste de las rocas en las zonas cercanas a la ruptura de la corteza terrestre.
